newsitem.title: UK: Powergen says expects to escape windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: Powergen says expects to escape windfall tax.

text.p: PowerGen Plc does not expect to have to pay any windfall profits tax levied by a future Labour government on the privatised utilities, chairman Ed Wallis said on Wednesday.
He told Parliament's Trade and Industry Committee that such a tax, if it were imposed, could impair the company's investment plans and cause it to look at its workforce levels.
"My best advice on what is likely to happen really comes from Mr (Labour leader Tony) Blair's office," Wallis told the committee.

"Blair seems to be putting forward a view which says if such a tax is to be applied, it will be applied to those who are in a monopoly business, those who are price regulated and those who have enjoyed the benefits of slack regulation."
"On all three counts, it does not apply to us."
However, Wallis added if PowerGen were brought within the scope of the proposed tax, the effects on the company would be "substantial".
"They would undoubtedly impair investment, they would undoubtedly cause us to look even more keenly at the number of people we employ," he said.
